requirement:
The SDK's `list_sources` result is discovery and
records neither the returned identity set nor the files' contents as
evidence inputs. Adding or removing a listed file therefore does not by
itself invalidate the evidence. Subsequent tracked reads record their own
dependencies.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.list_sources.inputs` has no structural obligation. It names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or named interface to delegate through. Its clauses are:

- "`list_sources` result is discovery"
- "records neither the returned identity set nor the files' contents as evidence inputs"
- "Adding or removing a listed file therefore does not by itself invalidate the evidence"

These clauses describe only what is observable. Evidence does not depend on the listing, and a changed file set does not invalidate it. The implementation can meet this in many ways. It might skip dependency tracking for `list_sources`, or record dependencies in some other structure. Any approach that leaves the evidence unchanged satisfies the text, so how it is built is discretionary.

The requirement has no implementation edges. It has one test edge, which is the right kind of evidence for behavior. No implementation root needs a reference.

behavioral: The requirement has two observable obligations. (1) A `list_sources` result records no evidence inputs, neither the returned identity set nor the file contents, so adding or removing a listed file does not invalidate evidence. (2) Subsequent tracked reads record their own dependencies.

Obligation 1 is covered by `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[listing_continuations_return_complete_paths_from_the_original_listing]`. It lists 2000 files plus an empty directory through a session and asserts `first.dependencies.is_empty()`. It then creates `added.rs` after the first listing, which is the add-a-file scenario. It pages through every continuation with `get_next_page` and asserts `delivery.dependencies.is_empty()` on each page. Any dependency on the identity set or on file contents would fail these assertions. The test also checks the returned files against the expected list, so the empty dependencies are not an artifact of an empty result.

The same test never removes a file. Removal is the same obligation as addition and goes through the same path: the listing result records nothing. The text does not say removal is handled differently.

Obligation 2 is exercised in `agent_node_addresses_round_trip_and_reject_inconsistent_identities_before_reads` in the same module. It asserts empty dependencies for `list_sources`. It then reads a node taken from the listing entry and compares that read's dependencies with those of reads by other addresses. Earlier in that test, `read_node` is asserted to record `expected("impl[Parser]")` as its own dependency. Per-read dependency tracking is a separate behavior from this requirement, so this is sufficient here.

I found no uncovered obligation or unacknowledged gap.
